clusters.mechanism: Runtime catalog mutations (PATCH/DELETE+re-add) leave ProviderTracker.modelBlocks keyed by the unchanged catalog ID, so the replacement backend inherits the old model's rejection block.
PATCH merges with the old definition and modelSchema rejects effort:null, so a model's default effort can never be cleared.
RuntimeCatalog.remove checks only operator routing cells, not the file/eval policy overlay, so deleting a model named there leaves the policy invalid and breaks the next startup.
Probe results are applied without a per-provider generation or ordering guard, so an older overlapping probe can overwrite newer discovery results.
Factory startup throws on stored runtime models that collide with config/code models or whose provider is gone, leaving the daemon unable to boot and the API unusable for removal.
The smoke script now opens and migrates the production DB and filters checks by provider-enabled overrides, so disabled providers' checks are silently dropped.
Every probe publishes provider status unconditionally (even when unchanged), and status() now queries SQLite on each call, adding SSE and DB overhead.
The existing smoke cleanup test (escaped-timeout) races with retries, appending extra PIDs before the assertion; this predates the change.
Eval runner builds targets directly and its availability guard ignores discovery exclusions, so evals invoke models the provider doesn't serve.
Queued chat calls choose a target before waiting for a slot and do not reroute or recheck served status after discovery changes.
The change exceeds the requested source-line budget, including out-of-scope smoke refactoring.
